title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Typical Cases Published by the People's Courts

I. Feng Hongfei Intentional Homicide Case

(1) Basic Facts

On December 9, 2011, the defendant Feng Hongfei and fellow villagers Feng A (victim, deceased, aged 13) and Feng B (victim, deceased, aged 13) agreed to go to a dam to catch mice, and later the three made barbecue together. During this time, Feng Hongfei quarreled with Feng A over a trivial matter, then used a long-handled knife and a hammer to stab and strike Feng A and Feng B successively, causing Feng A's heart to be pierced, resulting in hemorrhagic shock and death; and causing Feng B to die from hemorrhagic shock complicated by craniocerebral injury. Feng Hongfei dug a hole on the spot and buried the bodies of Feng A and Feng B. On December 11, to divert attention, Feng Hongfei wrote two ransom notes and placed them at the doorsteps of Feng A's and Feng B's homes.

(2) Judgment

The Supreme People's Court held that the defendant Feng Hongfei intentionally and unlawfully deprived others of their lives, and his conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide. Feng Hongfei killed two minors with weapons over a trivial matter, with cruel methods, particularly vile circumstances, and especially serious consequences, constituting extremely grave crimes, and should be punished according to law. The facts found in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance ruling were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, and the sentencing was appropriate. The trial procedures were lawful. In accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Supreme People's Court approved the criminal ruling of the Yunnan High People's Court affirming the first-instance judgment sentencing the defendant Feng Hongfei to death for intentional homicide, with deprivation of political rights for life.

(3) Typical Significance

In recent years, crimes infringing upon the rights and interests of minors have occurred from time to time, some being extremely serious and causing adverse social impact. For such crimes, courts nationwide have consistently adhered to strict crackdowns according to law, effectively punishing the criminals, and through case trials, enhancing the legal awareness and protective awareness of the whole society, further creating a favorable social environment conducive to the healthy growth of minors. In this case, the defendant Feng Hongfei killed two minors aged only 13 with a knife and a hammer over a trivial matter. His criminal methods were cruel, the circumstances were particularly vile, the consequences were especially serious, and the crime was extremely grave. The Supreme People's Court, based on Feng Hongfei's crimes, lawfully approved his death sentence, which was entirely correct.

II. Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch v. Shandong Iron and Steel Co., Ltd., Shandong Iron and Steel Co., Ltd., Jinan Branch, and Fujian Wanglong Trading Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Guarantee Warehouse Business Cooperation Contract

(1) Basic Facts

On February 24, 2012, Industrial Bank Jinan Branch, Wanglong Company, and Jigang Company signed the "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement on Guarantee Warehouse Business," stipulating: To ensure the performance of agreements under various credit business between Industrial Bank Jinan Branch and Wanglong Company during the period from February 24, 2012, to February 23, 2013, Wanglong Company and Jigang Company agreed to use bank acceptance drafts as the payment method for their trade contracts, with Industrial Bank Jinan Branch as the accepting bank of the drafts and Jigang Company as the payee of the drafts. Industrial Bank Jinan Branch agreed to lend to Wanglong Company to pay for the goods under the aforementioned trade contracts. The delivery of goods was to be carried out by Wanglong Company independently from Jigang Company. After the bank acceptance drafts were issued, Wanglong Company could extract from Jigang Company goods equal in value to 100% of the initial margin deposit. Thereafter, each time Wanglong Company extracted goods from Jigang Company, Jigang Company was required to do so only upon the "Delivery Notice" issued by Industrial Bank Jinan Branch. On the same day of receiving the "Delivery Notice," Jigang Company was to immediately issue a "Goods Dispatch Notice" to Industrial Bank Jinan Branch and handle the delivery of goods to Wanglong Company in accordance with the "Delivery Notice." If Jigang Company violated the above provisions and handled the delivery of goods to Wanglong Company, it should bear joint and several repayment liability to Industrial Bank Jinan Branch.

On February 27, 2012, Jigang Company changed its name to Shangang Company. On February 28, 2012, Shangang Jinan Company was established. Shangang Company agreed that Shangang Jinan Company would continue to perform the relevant responsibilities and obligations of Jigang Company under the "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement on Guarantee Warehouse Business," and the other two parties also acknowledged this.

On August 14, 2012, Industrial Bank Jinan Branch (acceptor) and Wanglong Company (acceptance applicant) signed the "Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Contract for Commercial Drafts." It stipulated that Industrial Bank Jinan Branch would handle bank acceptance drafts for Wanglong Company in the amount of RMB 81.5 million, with a term from August 14, 2012, to February 14, 2013. On August 15, 2012, Industrial Bank Jinan Branch delivered 17 bank acceptance drafts totaling RMB 81.5 million, with the drawer being Wanglong Company and the payee being Shangang Jinan Company, to Shangang Jinan Company, thereby fulfilling its obligations under the "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement on Guarantee Warehouse Business." Thereafter, without receiving a delivery notice from Industrial Bank Jinan Branch, Shangang Jinan Company failed to return the remaining RMB 57.05 million in acceptance drafts to Industrial Bank Jinan Branch as agreed in the "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement on Guarantee Warehouse Business," and instead delivered goods of equivalent value to Wanglong Company on its own.

The "Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Contract for Commercial Drafts" between Industrial Bank Jinan Branch and Wanglong Company matured on February 14, 2013, and Wanglong Company failed to perform its repayment obligations as agreed in the contract. As of March 25, 2013, Wanglong Company owed Industrial Bank Jinan Branch principal of RMB 56,707,177.04 and interest of RMB 1,081,765.24 in respect of bank acceptance draft advances.

Industrial Bank Jinan Branch filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting an order that Wanglong Company repay the sum of RMB 57.05 million under the bank acceptance drafts, and bear interest of RMB 1,081,765.24; and that Shangang Company and Shangang Jinan Company assume joint and several liability for the above debts.

(2) Judgment

The Shandong High People's Court held on second instance: The "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement on Guarantee Warehouse Business" signed by Industrial Bank Jinan Branch, Jigang Company, and Wanglong Company was to ensure the performance of various credit businesses between Wanglong Company and Industrial Bank Jinan Branch during the period from February 24, 2012, to February 23, 2013. According to the agreement, a trade contract relationship was established between Wanglong Company and Jigang Company. Wanglong Company, by applying to Industrial Bank Jinan Branch for the issuance of bank acceptance drafts as a financing method, had the bank acceptance drafts with Jigang Company as payee directly paid by Industrial Bank Jinan Branch to Jigang Company. Wanglong Company was to pay the full draft amount to Industrial Bank Jinan Branch before the maturity of the bank acceptance drafts. Industrial Bank Jinan Branch would issue a delivery notice to Jigang Company based on the amount and progress of Wanglong Company's payment, and Jigang Company would deliver goods to Wanglong Company according to the delivery notice issued by Industrial Bank Jinan Branch. If Jigang Company delivered goods to Wanglong Company without receiving a delivery notice from Industrial Bank Jinan Branch, it should bear joint and several repayment liability for Wanglong Company's debts. Subsequently, because Jigang Company changed its name to Shangang Company, the assets, liabilities, equity, business, and other rights and obligations of the original Jigang Company were succeeded by Shangang Jinan Company. Shangang Jinan Company failed to perform the "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement on Guarantee Warehouse Business" as agreed, constituting a breach of contract. Industrial Bank Jinan Branch's request for Shangang Jinan Company to bear joint and several repayment liability was in accordance with the contract and legal provisions. Therefore, Shangang Company should jointly with Shangang Jinan Company assume joint and several repayment liability for Wanglong Company's debts. Industrial Bank Jinan Branch advanced the bank acceptance draft amounts for Wanglong Company as agreed in the contract, fulfilling its contractual obligations. Wanglong Company failed to deposit the full draft amount with Industrial Bank Jinan Branch before the maturity of the bank acceptance drafts as agreed, and should bear repayment liability and pay interest as stipulated in the contract. Accordingly, the court ordered Wanglong Company to repay the principal of RMB 56,707,177.04 and interest of RMB 1,081,765.24 in respect of bank acceptance draft advances to Industrial Bank Jinan Branch; and Shangang Company and Shangang Jinan Company were to bear joint and several liability for Wanglong Company's repayment obligation.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is the first of its kind involving a guarantee warehouse dispute in Shandong Province, and the judgment served as a good demonstration effect. "Guarantee warehouse" refers to a financial service using bank credit as a carrier, bank acceptance drafts as a settlement tool, with the bank controlling the title to the goods, the seller holding the goods in trust and using a repurchase of the goods by the seller for the amount exceeding the margin deposit as a guarantee measure, and the bank providing bank acceptance drafts to the seller and the buyer. As a new type of financing method, the guarantee warehouse ensures payment for the seller, reduces financing costs for the buyer, and guarantees fund security for the bank. The judgment in this case fully reflects the functional role of the people's courts in supporting new types of financing methods and regulating the development of the financing market.

III. CCTV International Network Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai QuanTudou Culture Communication Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Infringement of the Right to Communicate Works through Information Network

(1) Basic Facts

"A Bite of China" is a large-scale food documentary produced by China Central Television. After its broadcast, it generated strong social impact and enjoyed high popularity. Subsequently, CCTV granted the copyright of the program to the plaintiff, CCTV International Network Co., Ltd. On May 23, 2012, upon the plaintiff's application, the Shanghai Jing'an Notary Office notarized the defendant Shanghai QuanTudou Culture Communication Co., Ltd.'s act of providing online on-demand streaming services of the work in question on its website "Tudou.com" (URL: www.tudou.com). The plaintiff argued that Tudou.com, without permission, provided online on-demand streaming services during the hot broadcast period of the work in question, seriously infringing its legitimate rights and interests and causing significant economic losses to the plaintiff. Therefore, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting an order that the defendant compensate economic losses of RMB 800,000 and reasonable expenses of RMB 50,000 for investigation and evidence collection.

(2) Judgment

The Minhang District People's Court of Shanghai and the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held after trial: The work in question is a work created by a method similar to film production as provided for in the Copyright Law of the PRC and should be protected under the Copyright Law. QuanTudou Company, without authorization, provided online on-demand streaming services of the work in question on its website during the work's hot broadcast period, which is a typical act of infringing the right to communicate works through information networks and should bear corresponding tort liability. QuanTudou Company argued that it provided storage space services and that the work in question was uploaded by netizens, but it did not provide evidence in support of this argument. Moreover, information about the actual uploader was within its own control and management, and it should have borne the burden of proof. Its deletion of the original data caused the relevant facts to be unascertainable, and it should bear the adverse consequences accordingly. Based on this, the court ordered QuanTudou Company to compensate CCTV Network Company RMB 240,000 for economic losses and RMB 8,000 for reasonable expenses.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is a typical example of a dispute over infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks on the Internet. The work in question reflects a high degree of originality and enjoys high social popularity. As a professional video-sharing website, Tudou.com is an influential professional network service provider. It disseminated the work in question without authorization during its hot broadcast period, and the infringement continued for a relatively long time, causing significant economic losses to the right holder. When determining the amount of statutory damages, the court fully considered factors such as the type of the work in question, its social popularity, the nature of the infringement, and the operational scale, mode, and influence of the infringing website, and awarded total compensation of RMB 248,000. This not only helps compensate the right holder for economic losses but also promotes self-discipline among various internet video providers and industry management. It also conforms to the trend of strengthening the protection of intellectual property rights on the Internet according to law and serves as a warning for the increasingly frequent internet video infringement cases.

IV. Guo Desheng v. Henan Weihui Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources — Administrative Penalty Dispute

(1) Basic Facts

In 2009, Guo Desheng built a livestock farm on land without going through the procedures for land use, actually occupying an area of 220.50 square meters of land. On December 5, 2011, the Henan Weihui Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources (hereinafter referred to as Weihui Land Bureau) issued an administrative penalty decision document No. Weiguotujianzi (2011) No. 041 against the plaintiff Guo Desheng, ordering the plaintiff to demolish the newly built buildings of 220.50 square meters on the illegally occupied 220.50 square meters of land, restore the land to its original condition, and impose a fine of RMB 4,410. The plaintiff argued that the facts found in the penalty decision were erroneous and filed a lawsuit with the Henan Weihui Municipal People's Court, requesting the revocation of the penalty decision.

(2) Judgment

The Henan Weihui Municipal People's Court held that the plaintiff Guo Desheng's act of illegally occupying land to build a livestock farm without approval violated the relevant provisions of the Land Administration Law of the PRC. The Weihui Land Bureau should, based on whether Guo Desheng's illegal occupation of land conformed to the local overall land use plan, impose an administrative penalty on Guo Desheng of either demolishing the buildings on the illegally occupied land within a time limit or confiscating the buildings on the illegally occupied land. However, the diagram provided by the defendant indicating the specific location of Guo Desheng's illegally occupied land was not accompanied by explanatory materials. During the trial, the defendant also failed to explain or clarify the method for determining the location of the land occupied by the plaintiff in the diagram, making it impossible for the court to determine whether the land occupied by Guo Desheng was agricultural land or construction land, that is, whether the livestock farm built by the plaintiff conformed to the local overall land use plan. This directly made it impossible to determine what penalty the defendant should impose on the plaintiff for the illegal act, that is, whether to demolish or confiscate the buildings on the illegally occupied land. At the same time, according to the Administrative Penalty Law and other provisions, before imposing a relatively heavy administrative penalty of ordering the demolition of buildings within a time limit on the plaintiff, the defendant should have made a collective discussion decision by the leaders of its own unit. However, the defendant did not provide evidence that the penalty decision against the plaintiff was made after a collective discussion by the leaders of its own unit. Therefore, the penalty decision made by the defendant against the plaintiff lacked sufficient main evidence and did not conform to legal procedures, and should be revoked according to law. In accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law, the court revoked the administrative penalty decision document No. Weiguotujianzi (2011) No. 041 issued by the Weihui Land Bureau on December 5, 2011, for the illegal land case against the plaintiff Guo Desheng, and ordered the defendant to handle the matter anew.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the first-instance judgment became legally effective.

(3) Typical Significance

Article 38, Paragraph 2 of the "Administrative Penalty Law" provides: "For relatively heavy administrative penalties imposed on complex or serious illegal acts, the responsible persons of the administrative organ shall make a collective discussion decision." Article 27 of the State Land Administration's "Measures for Investigating and Handling Illegal Land Cases" states: "Illegal land cases shall be collectively considered by the leaders of the land administration department, but the administrative chief responsibility system shall be implemented. Minutes of the consideration shall be made and signed by the members participating in the consideration..." The above provisions establish the system of collective discussion by the responsible persons of administrative organs in the administrative penalty procedure, that is, before imposing a relatively heavy penalty for complex or serious illegal acts, the responsible persons of the administrative organ shall conduct collective research through party group meetings, joint meetings, or chief executive meetings, and then make an administrative penalty decision.

Relatively heavy administrative penalties may have a significant impact on the rights of the person being penalized. For example, in this case, the land and resources department imposed a penalty of demolishing buildings within a time limit. Once executed, this penalty would cause irreversible consequences such as the loss of the building. Even if the penalty decision is later revoked through an administrative litigation procedure, it would no longer be possible to restore the original state. Through collective discussion by responsible persons, not only can the abuse of power by individual leading cadres be prevented, but also the democratic and scientific nature of administrative decisions can be ensured to the greatest extent, avoiding arbitrary decision-making.

V. Dai Shihua v. Jinan Public Security Fire Brigade — Fire Administrative Acceptance Dispute

(1) Basic Facts

On October 24, 2011, Jinan Old City Reconstruction Company submitted an acceptance filing application to the Jinan Public Security Fire Brigade, requesting a spot-check acceptance of the fire protection facilities for Buildings 1-8 of the shantytown renovation project south of Guanyi Street. After conducting a spot check, on November 21, 2011, the Jinan Public Security Fire Brigade issued the "Notice of Results of Fire Protection Acceptance Filing for Construction Projects" document No. Jigongxiaoyanbeibei (2011) No. 0172, determining that the spot check of the fire protection facilities for Buildings 1-8 of the shantytown renovation project south of Guanyi Street was qualified, and on the same day, the filing results were published on the "Shandong 365 Fire Service Network" under the fire supervision results section. Dai Shihua, a resident of Unit 3, Room 801, Building 6 of the project, believed that the installation of fire hydrant boxes in the building stairwell did not comply with fire safety installation standards, and that the facts found in the "Notice of Results of Fire Protection Acceptance Filing for Construction Projects" document No. Jigongxiaoyanbeibei (2011) No. 0172 were erroneous. He filed an administrative lawsuit with the Jinan High-tech Zone People's Court.

(2) Judgment

The Jinan High-tech Zone People's Court held on first instance: The "Notice of Results of Fire Protection Acceptance Filing for Construction Projects" is a technical acceptance notice, not a specific administrative act, and does not fall within the scope of administrative litigation of the people's courts. In accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law and other laws, the court ruled to dismiss the plaintiff Dai Shihua's lawsuit.

The Jinan Intermediate People's Court held on second instance: The fire protection acceptance filing for construction projects is the final step in the quality supervision and management of fire protection facilities for construction projects. The filing result includes an assessment of whether the fire protection completion acceptance is qualified. According to the provisions of the Fire Protection Law, construction projects that fail the fire protection acceptance by the public security fire protection organ must cease use. Accordingly, the results of the fire protection acceptance filing have binding force, and the act of fire protection acceptance filing has the nature of administrative confirmation. It is a specific administrative act of the fire protection administrative organ and falls within the scope of administrative litigation of the people's courts. In accordance with Article 68 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC," the court ruled to vacate the original ruling and order the Jinan High-tech Zone People's Court to continue the trial.

(3) Typical Significance

Currently, the situation regarding fire safety is unprecedentedly severe. As a front-line gateway for fire safety, the fire protection acceptance of construction projects carries significant responsibility, but it has long remained outside judicial review, leading to low public attention, poor procedural transparency, large arbitrariness in the exercise of power, and difficulty in fully exerting its role. This case clarified for the first time the nature of fire protection acceptance as an administrative confirmation, thereby bringing it within the scope of administrative litigation. This has important rule-making significance and will inevitably help supervise fire protection organs to strictly perform their acceptance duties, and is more conducive to ensuring the safety of people's lives and property. At the same time, through legal analysis and reasoning, the fire protection organ recognized the legitimacy of judicial review, actively prepared to participate in the subsequent litigation, and the court ultimately upheld the filing result notice. After the judgment was rendered, the case was intensively reported by important media outlets such as "Dazhong Daily" and "Jinan Daily," was included in Volume 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "China Administrative Trial Cases," and won the second prize for outstanding business achievements in national court administrative trials in 2013, achieving good legal and social effects.
